name: ERC Rule Explainer
blurb: what an ERC error means and its usual fix, in plain words
intro: Pick an ERC rule or paste the message your tool printed: you get what it means, the usual causes, the fix and when it is safe to waive. Rule codes and messages are KiCad 7/8's, with the Altium name of the same check; causes and fixes are common practice.

inputs.label: ERC rule
options: Input pin not driven by any Output pins
Input Power pin not driven by any Output Power pins
Pin conflict (e.g. Output pin connected to Output pin)
A pin with a "no connection" flag is connected
Label connected to only one pin
Global label only appears once in the schematic
Labels are similar (only differ in case)
More than one name given to this net
Symbol pin or wire end off connection grid
Four items connected at one point
Invalid connection between bus and net items
Net is graphically connected to a bus but not a bus member
Mismatch between hierarchical labels and sheet pins
Unit of a multi-unit symbol not placed
Missing input power pin in unit
Different footprints assigned to units of one part
Symbol library not found / symbol differs from library

inputs.label: Or paste the ERC message
inputs.placeholder: e.g. Input Power pin not driven by any Output Power pins
inputs.help: When it matches a rule, it overrides the pick above.

examples.title: The classic: power pin not driven

input.message: Label connected to only one pin

usage: Give the KiCad rule code (rule, e.g. power_pin_not_driven, pin_to_pin, label_dangling) or paste the ERC message text (message; it overrides rule when it matches). It returns the rule's message, the Altium name, how likely it is a real wiring bug, and a table with its meaning, usual causes, fix and when it may be waived, plus a filtered list of all rules. Use it while cleaning up an ERC report.
sources: KiCad 7/8 Eeschema documentation: Electrical Rules Check, ERC settings and pin conflict map
Altium Designer documentation: Project Options - Error Reporting and Connection Matrix
